title: Effect of Li Addition on Hardness and Microstructure in an A356 Al Alloy
content: The A356 alloy, mainly composed of aluminum, silicon, and magnesium, is a hypoeutectic alloy that has gained considerable importance in various industrial applications, particularly in the aerospace and automotive sectors. Its typical composition includes approximately 7 wt.% silicon and 0.3–0.4 wt.% magnesium provide excellent castability, mechanical properties, and corrosion resistance [1,2]. These alloys consist of primary α-Al dendrites [3,4] and acicular eutectic silicon [5,6], negatively affecting their mechanical properties and limiting their industrial applications. The addition of lithium (Li) to aluminum alloys, including A356, is primarily intended to reduce the alloy's density while enhancing its mechanical properties. Lithium decreases the density of aluminum alloys by approximately 3% for each 1 wt.% added, which is particularly beneficial in aerospace applications where weight reduction is crucial [7,8].
